title: Kris Bowers to Score Netflix's 'Steps,' a Cinderella Twist
summary:
Netflix's upcoming animated comedy 'Steps' just got a major musical upgrade. Emmy-nominated composer Kris Bowers is set to score the film, which puts a fresh twist on the story of Cinderella's evil stepsisters. The score was recorded in July and August 2026 at London's iconic Abbey Road Studios, and the movie is slated for release on November 20. It's also the first fully in-house animated feature from Netflix Animation Studios.

Bowers, known for his work on 'Green Book' and 'Bridgerton,' said he was hooked from the first conversation with directors Alyce Tzue and John Ripa. 'This story is incredibly written, incredibly acted, and incredibly animated,' he said. 'I feel so many layered emotions when I watch this film, and I'm just hoping that my music can speak to those feelings.'

The film follows Lilith (voiced by Ali Wong), who is blamed for hijacking the Royal Ball with a stolen magic wand. She accidentally turns her sister Margot (Stephanie Hsu) into a frog and leaves the kingdom in the hands of a prince-obsessed mean girl. Now Lilith must team up with Cinderella (Amanda Seyfried) and a surprisingly dreamy troll to save the kingdom and prove that even so-called 'villains' deserve a shot at happily-ever-after.

The voice cast is stacked: Bette Midler as the fairy godmother, Daniel Radcliffe as a royal, Young Mazino as 'The Heartthrob,' and Peter Dinklage as 'The Muscle.'

Tzue praised Bowers' collaborative spirit: 'Kris has this unique talent of being able to get into the heads and hearts of our characters. When he plays piano, it's like he draws a string from what he's feeling through the instrument to his audience.'

Tzue also shared that the story is personal: 'Growing up as an awkward, artsy Taiwanese kid in suburban New Jersey, I often felt like an outsider... I wanted to create a film for everyone who has ever felt like they didn't belong.' With Bowers' emotional score, 'Steps' promises to be a heartwarming and visually stunning adventure.
why_it_matters: 'Steps' reframes a classic fairy tale to show that everyone—even those labeled 'villains'—has a story worth telling, mirroring modern calls for empathy and second chances in a divided world.

background_read: Kris Bowers (an Emmy-nominated composer known for his jazz-infused scores for 'Green Book' and the TV series 'Bridgerton') is celebrated for blending classical techniques with modern emotions.

Abbey Road Studios (the iconic London recording venue immortalized by The Beatles' 1969 album of the same name) has hosted countless legendary film score recordings, from 'Star Wars' to 'Harry Potter.'
Netflix Animation Studios is the company's in-house animation division, launched to compete with Disney and DreamWorks; 'Steps' is its first full-length feature produced entirely on its own.
The traditional Cinderella story casts the stepsisters as irredeemable villains, but 'Steps' flips that trope, making them the flawed protagonists and exploring themes of redemption and belonging.

perspectives.description: Fans of reimagined fairy tales will celebrate a story that centers the stepsisters. The film offers a message about redemption and identity that resonates with anyone who has felt misunderstood, especially teens.
Some moviegoers might see 'Steps' as yet another attempt to cash in on a familiar IP by giving a villain a redemption arc—a formula that can feel worn out if not handled with genuine creativity.

The choice of Kris Bowers, a composer with a strong jazz and classical background, signals a commitment to emotional depth over generic cartoon music. Collaborations like this can elevate animated films into art that adults appreciate just as much as kids.

If successful, 'Steps' could inspire more studios to develop in-house animation teams and explore anti-hero narratives in family films. However, it also raises questions about whether audiences want a new take on every classic tale, or if some stories should be left alone.
